evals.prompt: During an EKS operations review, the user pasted a previous aws-eks-operations-review report for the same account, region, and cluster and asked what changed. Previous verdicts: S1 FAIL, S2 FAIL, R6 PASS, O12 FAIL; AX5 was not in the previous report. Current verdicts: S1 PASS, S2 FAIL, R6 FAIL, O12 N/A, AX5 FAIL. Per the skill's historical delta overlay, classify each, say how findings are matched between the two reports, and say where the delta appears in the report. No cluster access required.
evals.expected_output: S1 Resolved, S2 Persisting, R6 Regressed, O12 Unverified (FAIL to N/A is never Resolved), AX5 New. Matching uses fingerprints or check_id plus canonical_resource_id, never fuzzy titles; the prior report is used only from the conversation, never saved to a file.
assertions: The response classifies S1 as Resolved, S2 as Persisting, R6 as Regressed, and AX5 as New
The response classifies O12 as Unverified and explicitly not Resolved
The response states findings are matched by the finding fingerprint (or check_id plus canonical_resource_id), not by fuzzy title matching
The response places the delta in a 'Change since previous review' subsection of the executive summary

evals.prompt: During an EKS operations review the user asked which add-ons or images are vulnerable. Evidence already collected: AX5 shows vpc-cni is 3 minor versions behind the latest compatible version and coredns is current; S38 found Amazon Inspector enabled with zero CRITICAL/HIGH findings for images running in the cluster. Which grading guard applies, what may the report say about vpc-cni, and which CVEs affect that vpc-cni version? No cluster access required.
evals.expected_output: Guard FP13 applies to AX5/S38. The vpc-cni lag is reported as a version gap, not a vulnerability, and no CVE, CVSS score, or vulnerable version is named because none appears in a retrieved Inspector finding or AWS security bulletin. Customer Inspector findings do not cover AWS-hosted add-on images, so the report points to the add-on release notes and AWS security bulletins.
assertions: The response names grading guard FP13 as the guard that applies
The response labels the vpc-cni lag as a version gap rather than a confirmed vulnerability
The response names no CVE identifier or CVSS score for vpc-cni
The response states customer Inspector findings do not cover AWS-hosted add-on images and points to add-on release notes or AWS security bulletins

evals.prompt: During an EKS operations review, the user asks to compare dev-cluster, staging-cluster, and prod-cluster for drift. They pasted last week's aws-eks-operations-review report for dev-cluster, have no report for staging-cluster, and asked you to review prod-cluster live now. Assume the prod-cluster review completed with QA PASS. Parity verdicts: AX11 dev PASS / prod FAIL; S15 dev FAIL / prod FAIL; S28 dev FAIL / prod PASS; AX10 dev PASS / prod N/A. Per the skill's comparison overlay, classify each, say what happens to staging-cluster, and describe how the result is delivered. No cluster access required.
evals.expected_output: AX11 Production-only gap, S15 Systemic, S28 Lower-environment gap, AX10 Not comparable. staging-cluster is not reviewed live in this conversation, because a comparison reviews at most one cluster live; it is listed as Not compared until the user supplies a report from a separate review. prod-cluster keeps its own complete report, and the comparison is a separate EKS Fleet Comparison deliverable. Drift classes never change per-cluster severity.
assertions: The response classifies AX11 as a production-only gap and S15 as systemic
The response classifies S28 as a lower-environment gap and AX10 as not comparable
The response does not start a second live review for staging-cluster and lists it as not compared until a report is supplied
The response states the comparison is a separate deliverable from prod-cluster's own complete report
The response states at most one cluster is reviewed live and the other clusters come from supplied reports

evals.prompt: For a plain full EKS operations review where the user never mentioned prior reports or other clusters, does the skill load the overlays reference or add any overlay subsection? No cluster access required.
evals.expected_output: No. The ledger records overlays: none, overlays.md is not loaded, and the report contains only the eight mandatory sections without overlay subsections.
assertions: The response states overlays.md is not loaded when no overlay is requested
The response states the ledger records overlays: none
The response states the eight mandatory report sections are unchanged
